title: Rav Ila
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Menachot 81a: “Rav Ila fell ill; Abaye and the Rabbis went in to visit him.” Shitah Mekubbetzet reads “Rav Ila bar Abba,” but Hyman considers the Dikdukei Soferim reading more correct: “Rav Ulla”; so too in the Venice printings of רפ״ט and ש״ח.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The heading’s ד״ה א׳ פ״יא־כט is read as I Chronicles 11:29, pointing to the form Ili (עילי). This is a name comparison, not a claim that the sage is the biblical figure.

עול in חלש עול לגביה is “entered”: the sick sage receives Abaye and the sages. Hyman distinguishes Ila, Ila bar Abba in Shitah Mekubbetzet, and Ulla in Dikdukei Soferim; his preference for Ulla is retained as his judgment.

דק״ס is conventionally read Dikdukei Soferim. רפ״ט and ש״ח in the Venice-printing reference are read as years [5]289 and [5]308, corresponding to 1528/29 and 1547/48. This numerical reading does not independently verify the editions or their wording.
